narrative.overview:
The site is a weekly, and the homepage is this week's issue. The newest episode is the cover story: a blue block carrying its title in very large type, a deck, two actions and the thumbnail in a white frame. Everything older is back issues, listed as numbered rows and reached through one archive panel. Above the cover sits an issue bar ("Edisi 189 · 11 November 2026" on the left, the broadcast schedule on the right) under a 2px ink rule, the way a paper dates its front page.

The ground is a cool light paper (`#f1f2f6`) with white cards and navy ink (`#14183a`). Two hues sit on it, and `src/styles/global.css` records where each came from: the blue is the podcast cover's band darkened until it carries white type, and the orange is the title strip on every episode thumbnail. Blue means a reader can act on something, and it owns the one drenched surface on the site, the homepage cover block. Orange is decoration: the 3px rules over the key points, icon fills, a faint tint. Purple, which the previous palette carried, is gone from the stylesheet. The subscribe button in the navigation stays YouTube red, a platform's colour quoted as a citation.

One typeface does everything. Archivo ships as a single self-hosted variable file with a width axis, and the `.display` class pushes it wide and heavy for the wordmark, the cover title, the homepage section headings and the episode numerals. The episode page uses the same voice for its title and section headings. The archive, topic, about, subscribe and partners pages have not taken it yet: their titles are plain 700. All of them share the palette, the hairlines and the episode card.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground, white cards, navy ink, hairline rules
One blue with three steps for acting, one orange that only decorates
A single drenched surface: the blue cover block on the homepage
Archivo throughout; `.display` (118% width, weight 800) as the masthead voice
Rules and numbered rows on the homepage, the 16:9 card grid on archive pages
Monospace for transcript timecodes and other machine-flavoured text

rules.name: The Two-Job Rule
rules.body: Blue means *you can act on this*. Orange means *look here*, and it only decorates. A new element takes the hue that describes its job. A link, a button or an active state is blue; a rule, an accent stroke or a tint may be orange.

rules.name: The Fill/Type Split
rules.body: Each hue has steps and they are not interchangeable. For blue: `accent-strong` fills shapes that carry type, `accent-text` colours type, bare `accent` is for icons, tints and borders. For orange the split is a contrast matter: the sampled value is 2.15:1 under white and 1.9:1 on the ground, so type takes `highlight-text` and a fill that carries white takes `highlight-strong`.

rules.name: The One Drench Rule
rules.body: Exactly one surface on the site is flooded with the accent: the homepage cover block. Inside it everything takes the `on-accent` tokens, and the `.on-accent` class switches the focus ring to white because the blue ring disappears on blue.

rules.name: The Hover Rule
rules.body: A filled blue control hovers to `accent-hover`: the ink navy in light, a brighter blue in dark. Hover never changes the hue family.

rules.name: The Borrowed-Colour Rule
rules.body: Platform Red belongs to YouTube. Spotify green (`#1DB954`), the RSS orange and the share row's brand fills belong to their platforms too: reproduce the brand value and choose the label colour that clears AA on it. The Spotify tile is labelled in black for that reason (the stylesheet comment on `/subscribe` records 2.59:1 for white against 8.12:1 for black).

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo is the only webfont and it is one file. A second voice comes from the width and weight axes, never from a second family. The exceptions are surfaces that cannot load it: `public/offline.html`, `public/favicon.svg` and the build-time share cards stay on the system `sans-serif`.

rules.name: The Masthead Rule
rules.body: `.display` is for nameplates, page and section headings, and numerals. It sets width, weight, tracking and balance; the size stays on the element. Running text, labels and controls never take it.

rules.name: The Ink Ladder Rule
rules.body: Every block of text picks one rung: `ink` for headings, `ink-body` for prose, `ink-muted` for secondary copy, `ink-subtle` for metadata. The contrast test asserts the four stay in descending order.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Numbers that line up or change (dates, durations, counts, the issue bar, the audio clock) take `tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Flat Floor Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and separated by hairlines or by a step in tone.

rules.name: The Two Step Rule
rules.body: There are two steps off the paper: the white card and the overlay tint. The overlay is for things that sit over the page or respond to the pointer (the mobile menu, the skip link, a hover fill). There is no popover, modal or drawer precedent in the build.

rules.name: The Whole-Card Target Rule
rules.body: An episode card or row is one link. Nothing interactive nests inside it; the offline indicator is decorative for that reason.

rules.name: The Visible Focus Rule
rules.body: `:focus-visible` in `global.css` draws a `2px` Blue Ink outline at `2px` offset on everything, and a white one inside `.on-accent`. A component may add to it. Nothing may remove it without putting something at least as visible in its place.

dos: Do build new surfaces from the tokens: white card on paper with a `1px` hairline, or the overlay tint for something that sits over the page.
Do make every filled control Blue Fill with `on-accent` type and a hover to `accent-hover`.
Do put anything that lives on the cover block inside `.on-accent` and use `on-accent` and `on-accent-muted` for its type.
Do use `.display` for a nameplate, a section heading or a numeral, and set the size on the element.
Do carry hierarchy with the ink ladder before reaching for size.
Do reuse the `1 → 2 → 4` episode grid with a `1.5rem` gutter on archive pages, so archive, topic and year pages stay one product.
Do restate a moved token in `public/offline.html`, `public/favicon.svg` and `src/lib/partner-card.ts`, or read it through `src/lib/palette.ts`.
Do write every user-facing label in Bahasa Indonesia.
donts: Don't put full-strength Thumbnail Orange under type or use it to fill a control; it measures 2.15:1 under white.
Don't colour type with bare `highlight`; type takes `highlight-text`.
Don't drench a second surface in the accent. The cover block is the one.
Don't bring purple or a third accent hue back. Platform Red and the other brand colours are citations.
Don't add a second webfont, and don't load Archivo from a third party; the site ships one self-hosted file.
Don't add a shadow to anything at rest.
Don't put an interactive element inside an episode card or row.
Don't use anything quieter than `ink-subtle` for text that carries meaning, and don't write a hex literal where a token exists.
Don't use `system-ui` in anything rasterised at build time; it resolves to nothing on the Linux build agent.
